LESSON: LANGUAGE WELCOME AND

Grade: Grade 1
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Language Welcome and

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Language Welcome and. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What is your name?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. 

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: LANGUAGE WELCOME AND
Subject: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Language Welcome and helps you succeed in ENGLISH ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: LANGUAGE WELCOME AND
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. 

What this means
In this part you learn to recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. . You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. .
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Language Welcome and”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. . Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Language Welcome and is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Language Welcome and”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. )

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Language Welcome and to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. .
3. Make one local Kenya example of Language Welcome and from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Language Welcome and: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 1 learner study Language Welcome and?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What is your name?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Language Welcome and means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognise the present tense verb ‘to be’ I am a boy, I am a for the forms of the verb ‘to be’ in girl development of sentences. .

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
